To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“The contact strain which develops during compression-folding in a host rock of a more “ competent ” layer is negligible outside a zone of the order of the initial wavelength on either side of a folded sheet, and this conclusion is also valid for rather strong initial buckling.”
the wavelength of a folded multilayer is a function of the spacing between the layers, and the wavelength is greater for closer spacing.

the initial stable wavelength in a multilayer is a function of the thickness of the layers, of the mechanical properties of the layers, and of the spacing of the competent layers, and that the spacing of the layers is an important parameter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of buckling of thin layers in a multilayer system under compression.
the buckling of multilayered bodies.
the buckling and folding of thin and thick layers under compression and with the strain distribution in folded layers and folded multilayers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the theory of buckling under compression of a multilayers consisting alternating competent and incompetent layers is not yet sufficiently developed to permit any general conclusion as to the wavelength/thickness ratios which will actually develop in the earth.
the thick-layer theory of viscous folding is the most realistic of the theories presented in this paper.

, for a multilayer, the initial stable wavelength is a function of the thickness and mechanical properties of the layers, the spacing between them, and the mechanical properties of the uniform surrounding material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theory of buckling and folding of multilayers of alternating competent and incompetent layers has been developed in some details.
the thick-layer theory is more realistic than the thin-layer theory and gives results which agree better with experimental tests.

, if a multilayer is sandwiched between two thick layers of a less “competent substance” (or if it is embedded in a large uniform mass of such a substance), it will buckle in the sense that the wavelength will be of the order of the thickness of the competent layers and that the amplitude of the folds will be of the same order of magnitude as the wavelength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the contact strain which develops during compression-folding can be neglected outside a zone of one initial wavelength on either side of a folded competent layer.
the contact strain and folding instability are important factors to consider in the study of multilayered rock bodies.

the contact strain is negligible outside the zone about one initial stable wavelength wide on either sides of the folded sheet and this theoretical conclusion based upon contact deformation resulting from initial small-amplitude buckle is valid for strong buckle as well.
